name: Canva
headline: Direct WebP export for web creators.
summary: I researched a WebP export proposal and created the team’s presentation slides.

sections.label: Context
sections.text: Collaborative product teardown.

sections.label: My contribution
sections.text: I researched the WebP export feature proposal and created the presentation slides using Canva.

sections.label: Problem identified in the 2025 analysis
sections.text: The team identified a need for users preparing web images to avoid separate conversion tools.

sections.label: Recommendation
sections.text: Offer direct WebP export to Canva Pro users to simplify preparation of lighter web-ready images. Benefits were expected outcomes, not tested or delivered results.

sections.label: Tools
sections.text: Canva for presentation slides.

sections.label: Deliverables
sections.text: WebP feature research and presentation slides. The separate bank-transfer proposal was wider team work.

sections.label: Status
sections.text: Teardown and proposed feature. Expected benefits were not tested or shipped.

name: Uber vs Bolt
headline: Two journeys. Different product choices.
summary: A comparison of strategy, positioning and user experience, with recommendations for both platforms.

sections.label: Context
sections.text: Individual comparative teardown.

sections.label: My work
sections.text: I compared their beginnings, strategies, unique selling points, user reviews and positioning, and developed recommendations based on the analysis.

sections.label: Recommendations explored
sections.text: Affordability, app performance, driver satisfaction, clearer pricing and local relevance for Uber; mapping accuracy, payment reliability, safety, cancellations, support and stability for Bolt.

sections.label: Tools
sections.text: Google Workspace and Canva.

sections.label: Deliverables
sections.text: Comparative analysis, visual comparison and product recommendations.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.text: An independent assessment of product choices and improvement opportunities. These are findings from the 2025 analysis, rather than implemented changes or current safety and reliability rankings.

name: Claude AI
headline: More locally relevant AI proposals.
summary: I co-supervised the team alongside another supervisor. My contributions included affordability guidance for Nigerian users and presentation review.

sections.label: Context
sections.text: Team teardown jointly supervised by me and another supervisor; not employment at Anthropic.

sections.label: My contribution
sections.text: I was one of two supervisors on this project. We jointly supervised and reviewed the team’s work on Claude’s background, problem, evolution, value proposition, audience, positioning, features, survey feedback and competitor benchmarking. My personal contributions included guiding affordability recommendations for Nigerian users and reviewing the presentation. The wider analysis was the team’s work.

sections.label: A decision I influenced
sections.text: The early survey-based suggestions were generic. I challenged the team to consider barriers affecting Nigerian users, helping focus the recommendation on affordability and a proposed Claude Mini plan. The team also proposed international phone-number verification support.

sections.label: Presentation review
sections.text: I corrected the presentation flow and requested persona, user flow and roadmap visuals to explain the recommendations more clearly.

sections.label: Tools
sections.text: Google Workspace and Canva.

sections.label: Deliverables
sections.text: Review feedback, refined feature recommendations and presentation guidance. Personas, flows and roadmap were team outputs I requested and reviewed, not sole-authored work.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.text: A more focused team proposal, developed by the team with joint supervision. Features were recommendations, not shipped changes. The analysis does not establish current pricing or verification limitations.

name: Let’sChat
headline: What would a thoughtful recovery take?
summary: Failure analysis and a proposed three-phase roadmap, starting with trust and reliability.

sections.label: Context
sections.text: Independent teardown of an Africa-focused messaging app.

sections.label: My contribution
sections.text: I investigated what went wrong and identified trust, security and technical reliability as major concerns in my analysis. I developed a proposed recovery plan and implementation roadmap.

sections.label: Tools
sections.text: Notion for documentation; Google Search and ChatGPT for research support.

sections.label: Deliverables
sections.text: Failure analysis, recovery proposal and phased implementation roadmap.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.text: A proposed sequence from reliability to relevant differentiation and revenue. This was an analytical recovery proposal, not a delivered recovery or relaunch.

roadmap.title: Restore stability
roadmap.text: Fix bugs and crashes, simplify signup and verification, improve call quality.

roadmap.title: Differentiate
roadmap.text: Low-data usage, offline messaging, AI summaries and translation, social sharing, mobile-money integration and community calling.

roadmap.title: Sustainable revenue
roadmap.text: Explore premium features, local advertising and telecom partnerships.
